TSNA Priority Program

-Conditions were established for the removal of TSNA and alkaloids from filler by solvent extraction. Lower polarity solvents give the best selectivity for the removal of TSNA and alkaloids with respect to dry weight.

-A time course study of TSNA formation during curing of bright and burley tobaccos was completed. TSNA levels in burley tissue after curing are correlated with the nitrate levels in the tissues, but not the alkaloid levels. A reduction in TSNA formation can be achieved by treatment of burley with ascorbate or \(\alpha\)-tocopherol before curing.

-Levels of nitrate nitrogen appear to be more relevant to the development of filler NNN and NAT than filler NNK for greenhouse-grown bright tobacco.

Decreases in filler TSNA content were observed after the extraction of filler with supercritical carbon dioxide. These reductions were obtained when carbon, cocoa shells, and a variety of stem products were utilized as nicotine adsorbers. Several methods for the destruction of the TSNA on the various adsorbers were investigated. Heat treatment was determined to be the method of choice. TSNA were detected in a wax sample from an extraction vessel.

Addition of stem used as nicotine adsorber in the SCFE of filler to RLTC and RL 150B did not significantly increase the MS TSNA delivery of either RL with respect to the MS TSNA delivery from the appropriate control.

Treatment of tobacco with liquid carbon dioxide (DIET process) does not result in detectable changes in TSNA levels.

- The time course of TSNA synthesis and decomposition in aqueous solutions under model conditions, in the presence and absence of nitrite, was studied.
- The time course of TSNA synthesis is a result that is used to determine the time constant for 40 seconds decay rate.

-Model studies of the thermal decomposition of TSNA were conducted to evaluate the effect of antioxidants on TSNA decomposition. Results of this work indicated that the reduction of MS NNN observed when AP is added to filler may be due to enhanced NNN decomposition, rather than inhibition of pyrosynthesis. Studies with NNK are incomplete.
